extraction_metadata.extraction_notes: Vector table with a clean text layer. Column boundaries and every merged span were taken from rule-line geometry recovered from a 200 dpi raster render (identical on both grid pages: 26 vertical rules -> 1 label column + 24 data columns); marks were binned to those columns from pdftotext -bbox token centres and diffed against a visual read of the rendered pages. One leading label column (L=1), so the first data column is position 2. Document pages taken from PAGEMAP.md (PDF pages 1-4 = document pages 14-17); the printed footers happen to agree.

table_metadata.table_purpose: Main schedule of activities for the whole study: screening, check-in, inpatient Period 1, outpatient period, inpatient Period 2, unscheduled visits and End of Study/Early Termination.
table_metadata.notes: Single logical table; the grid runs across document pages 14-15 with the three header rows reprinted verbatim on page 15, and the footnote block runs from page 15 into page 16, so page 16 contributes annotations but no activity rows. Header rows 1-2 have no printed row label (the label column carries 'Study Procedures' merged over both), so both property names are synthesized. Transcribed as printed, not repaired: (1) the 'Inpatient Period 2' cell in header row 2 spans columns 15-23 (Days 24-40) and the Day 23 column (position 14) has an EMPTY period cell, although footnote v states inpatient Period 2 runs Day 23 to Day 40; (2) the activity 'PD: Plasma total and PUF-Cu, LBC, ceruloplasmin, ceruloplasmin-bound Cu' (row 31, first body row on page 15) carries no marks in the source - the marks for the PK/PD sampling pair are printed only on the preceding row 'Blood sampling for PK: Plasma total Mo and PUF-Mo' (row 30, last body row on page 14). In Table 2 the same two assessments share one merged mark cell, so the empty row is probably a vertical merge broken by the page break, but the page break makes the merge unverifiable from rule-line geometry and the marks were left where they are printed.

schedule_properties.property_comment: Topmost header row. The row label cell is empty (the label column carries 'Study Procedures', merged over header rows 1-2), so the name is synthesized. The row carries visit/encounter designations - 'Screening' (merged over the two screening day columns), 'C-I' (check-in), 'UNS' (unscheduled) and 'EOS or ET' (End of Study or Early Termination) - with one empty merged cell spanning columns 5-23. Typed 'visit' because its values name encounters rather than study phases; it is the only row that distinguishes the UNS column from its neighbours.

Second header row; label cell empty (shared 'Study Procedures' cell), so the name is synthesized. Values are the study's periods - Screening, C-I, Inpatient Period 1, OP (outpatient), Inpatient Period 2 - each spanning several day columns. Typed 'period' because the values are named sub-phases of the study ('Period 1'/'Period 2' are the source's own words) rather than visits or days.

Printed row label 'Days'. Values are protocol study days and day ranges relative to first dose (-42 to -9, -21, -8, -7, -6 through -5, -4 through -1, 1, 2-3 ... 40), plus an empty cell under UNS and 'EOS Day 54+/-2' under the EOS or ET column. Typed 'study_day' because every value is a protocol day or day range.

annotations.annotation_text: Within 42 days of ALXN1840 administration. Details of procedures that may be performed by sites designated as “screening sites” (only in the US) are detailed in Section 8.
Participants will be admitted to the clinical research unit (CRU) at least 10 hours prior to enrollment and initiation of copper- and molybdenum-controlled diet.
At the CRU’s discretion, participants may remain in the CRU or be readmitted on Day 22 with all procedures starting on Day 23.
Unscheduled study visits may occur at any time during the study and may include any study procedure as deemed necessary by the Investigator.
Participants are required to return to the CRU Day 54+/-2; participants will be discontinued from ALXN1840 medication by their physician at the latest by the Day 54 follow-up.

Discharge from the unit may occur after completion of all procedures on Day 9 and on Day 40 and after the Investigator has reviewed all safety assessment (including safety laboratory tests) and confirmed that the participant is appropriate for discharge.

A single outpatient visit or phone call and safety laboratory assessment should occur between Day 14 and Day 18. A phone call may take place on a different day than the blood draw within the Day 14 through Day 18 period.
If needed to confirm menopause.
Parameters include age and sex. Race and ethnicity will be collected where permitted by local regulations.
Wilson disease history will include diagnosis date, method of diagnosis, history of cirrhosis, details of any previous liver biopsies performed, and treatment received.

A full physical examination will be performed at Screening, at check-in for the study, and at the End of the study/Early Termination Visit. A physical examination should also be performed on any participants with ongoing adverse events prior to discharge from the unit. Otherwise, a symptom-driven physical examination may be performed at other times, at the Principal Investigator’s discretion.
Height at screening only.

While in the CRU, study intervention will be administered after an overnight fast (ie, at least 10 hours) at the same time every morning; drug is to be administered with 240 mL of water and meals should be delayed a minimum of 2 hours after dosing. As an outpatient, participants are expected to take ALXN1840 at approximately the same time daily (+/-1 hour). Participants should take the medication with a glass of water on an empty stomach; meals should be delayed a minimum of 2 hours after dosing.
During the outpatient period, participants will use SMS text messaging to confirm study intervention administration.
Blood sampling for PK/PD will occur before ALXN1840 administration and represents a predose trough. See Table 2 for PK/PD sampling on Days 1, 25, 29, and 39.
PK/PD collection will include timepoints described in the schedule of PK/PD assessment for Days 1, 25, 29, and 39 (Table 2).

Samples for serum chemistry will be obtained following a fast of at least 8 hours at the Screening Visit and at check-in. In case of rechecks, and postdose serum chemistry, participants may not have fasted for 6 or 8 hours before the serum chemistry sample is taken.
Laboratory assessment including chemistry, hematology, and coagulation parameters should be performed on Days -8, -1, 8, 23, and 28 only.

Menstruation check is for women only; women of childbearing potential should only be enrolled after a negative serum pregnancy test result at Screening. Additional urine pregnancy testing will be standard for the protocol unless serum testing is required by site policies, local regulation, or Institutional Review Boards (IRBs)/Independent Ethics Committees (IECs) (Section 10.2). In addition to pregnancy tests detailed at the visits in the SoA, females of childbearing potential will be required to perform urine pregnancy tests at least every 4 weeks at their home or the study site throughout their time in the study.
A single 15 mL serum sample will be retained for evaluation in the event of an unexpected safety finding; retained samples may be destroyed after completion of the clinical study report.

Vital signs measurements and ECGs should be performed predose, unless otherwise specified. Vitals signs include body temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, and systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

Copper- and molybdenum-controlled diet will be initiated after registration/inclusion. Participants will remain on a copper/molybdenum controlled diet throughout both the inpatient Period 1 (Day -8 to Day 9) and inpatient Period 2 (Day 23 to Day 40); during this time participants will be strongly encouraged to complete all meals. While not in the CRU, participants will be encouraged to adhere to their usual copper-controlled diet.
For each input/output balance period, 24-hour urine samples are to be collected for measurement of copper and molybdenum.
For fecal samples, each individual sample will be independently collected with record of date, time, and weight of the sample.
